description: The oldest poster on any wall in Freedom City, and it looks it: institutional pulp gone the colour of weak tea, four generations of staples through the corners, each printing pasted over the last so the man has depth to him, like sediment. It is laid out exactly as a public health notice and it is not one. A figure stands square to the viewer with his mouth open on a single syllable and his arms spread in what the artist plainly intended as benediction, and behind him the crowd has already caught it: every face in the receding ranks is open on the same word, rank behind rank, smaller and smaller toward the vanishing point until the mouths stop being mouths and become a grey wash of it, and the wash keeps going, past the edge of the paper, past the wall. DJERK SAID IT ONCE. Beneath, in the flat unhurried serif of a quarantine bulletin: "ONE UTTERANCE. NO KNOWN VECTOR. NO KNOWN CURE. NO SERIOUS ATTEMPT MADE TO FIND ONE." A pathology credit runs along the bottom margin in six-point type, the way a painter signs a corner, "cultured by EAZY", and at his shoulder in every printing stands a second figure nobody ever captioned, thin as a thread and half a step behind him, patient as something waiting on a web. The left edge is factory-clean, a true printed margin. Every other edge is torn, as though this sheet was only ever meant to be the beginning of something much wider.
name: hero poster: DJERK, THE FIRST WORD
